cards.explanation: The answer is a man or a woman. The LORD tells Moses to say, "…if a man or woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to separate himself to the LORD…" (Numbers 6:2). Nobody needs a title, a tribe or a fancy hat for this one, friends. I own a very tall hat and it still doesn't count for anything here.

The answer is False. Wine isn't the only thing on the list, friends. The text says he "…must not drink any grape juice or eat fresh grapes or raisins." (Numbers 6:3). Then it adds that he's not to eat anything from the grapevine, "…not even the seeds or skins." (Numbers 6:4). The LORD covers the whole vine, top to bottom.

The word is razor. For the entire period of his vow, "…no razor shall touch his head." (Numbers 6:5). The text says he "…must let the hair of his head grow long." That's the whole vow, start to finish, friends. I'd say that razor is going to sit in a drawer feeling real left out.

The answer is False. I think this is one of the hardest lines in the passage, friends. The text says, "Even if his father or mother or brother or sister should die, he is not to defile himself…" (Numbers 6:7). No exception is given for family. The reason is that the symbol of consecration to his God is upon his head.

The answer is that his head carries the sign of his vow to God. The text says, "…because the symbol of consecration to his God is upon his head." (Numbers 6:7). That's the reason it gives, even when the dead is family, friends. His head carries the sign of his vow, and that is why he keeps his distance from the dead.

The answer is to shave his head. If someone suddenly dies in his presence and defiles his consecrated hair, "…he must shave his head on the day of his cleansing…" (Numbers 6:9). That's the seventh day. All that growing, and the hair has to come off anyway, friends. I think that one hurts.

The answer is seventh. If someone suddenly dies in his presence, he must shave his head on the day of his cleansing, the seventh day (Numbers 6:9). Then the eighth day brings the birds for the priest (Numbers 6:10). Seven days of waiting while that hair sits there defiled, friends. I think I'd be checking the mirror every morning.

The answer is True. The priest offers one bird as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and then the text says, "On that day he must consecrate his head again." (Numbers 6:11). A fresh start for his head, friends. The vow starts over, too.

The answer is that they no longer count. The text says, "But the preceding days shall not be counted, because his separation was defiled." (Numbers 6:12). He rededicates his time of separation to the LORD and starts over, friends. It's like a whole batch of dough dumped on the floor and the timer set back to zero.

The answer is fire. The Nazirite is "…to shave his consecrated head, take the hair, and put it on the fire under the peace offering." (Numbers 6:18). So the long hair ends up on the fire, under the offering, friends. After all that growing, that's quite the finish.

The answer is the priest. After the wave before the LORD, the text says, "This is a holy portion for the priest…" (Numbers 6:20). That's in addition to the breast of the wave offering and the thigh that was presented. I think that priest is walking out with a full cookie box and zero complaints, friends.

The answer is True. The text says, "After that, the Nazirite may drink wine." (Numbers 6:20). That comes after the shave and the wave offering. The time of separation is complete (Numbers 6:13). Patience pays off, friends.

The answer is that he must fulfill it. The text says, "he must fulfill whatever vow he makes, according to the law of his separation." (Numbers 6:21). If you make the promise, you keep it, friends. It's as simple as saying you'll bring the cookies and then actually bringing the cookies.
